title: Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP)

scope.purpose: Define the governed master information delivery plan aggregating task-team TIDPs and their information containers, delivery milestones, states, information need, permitted use, responsibilities and review/acceptance dependencies.

requirements.statement: The authoring party shall not serve as sole approver for a MIDP entry where a separate governed review, authorization or acceptance responsibility applies.

Where ISO 19650-2 applies, the lead appointed party shall establish and maintain the delivery team's MIDP by aggregating the TIDPs from the task teams. A TIVERIT or project job title may perform this function only where the appointment, BEP, RACI or equivalent governing project instrument assigns that responsibility.
Information deliverables shall be scheduled with unique deliverable identifiers matching the governed CDE information-container naming requirements.
Every MIDP line item shall trace to at least one constituent TIDP entry and its governed information container or deliverable.

Where ISO 19650 applies, MIDP means Master Information Delivery Plan. Information containers such as Revit models are planned within contributing TIDPs and aggregated into the MIDP; the acronym shall not be expanded as Model Information Delivery Plan in ISO-aligned TIVERIT use.

runtime_note: The L4 MIDP standard defines governed rules and fields. Runtime MIDP instances in the BEP delivery engine are implementation data, not a replacement for this standard. Project BIM Manager remains a TIVERIT role and is not assumed to be the ISO lead appointed party without project-specific authority mapping.

provenance.migration_note: Source-era title used Model Information Delivery Plan. Curator correction aligns the canonical TIVERIT term to ISO 19650-2:2018 clause 5.4.5: Master Information Delivery Plan. Existing container-delivery intent is preserved; task-team TIDPs identify information containers and the lead appointed party aggregates them into the MIDP where ISO 19650-2 applies.
